---
title: "Lab · Trace the outer delivery loop against real tooling"
---

::: {.callout-note title="Scaffold — paper walkthrough, not runnable end-to-end"}
This lesson does **not** ship a new reusable lab. The runnable
pieces the academy publishes today cover one segment of the outer
loop each:

- Stage 0 (hand-off) — runnable via the
  [Sandcastle → Kubernetes hand-off lab](../../../../labs/handoff-sandcastle-to-kubernetes/).
- Stage 4 (Crossplane reconciliation) — runnable via the
  [Hello Pico on Kubernetes lab](../../../../labs/hello-pico-on-kubernetes/).
- Stages 1–3 (review, merge, GitOps delivery) — inspectable in
  this repository and any GitOps setup you already have, but not
  yet packaged as a single automatable lab.

The steps below are therefore an **inspection walkthrough**: you
map each outer-loop stage onto artifacts you can already see, and
you note where a runnable extension would slot in later.
:::

## What you will do

Walk each outer-loop stage against something concrete: the branch
from the previous lab, this repository's CI, and the Crossplane
apply from the Kubernetes lab. At the end you will have a written
picture of what is runnable today and what is scaffolded.

## Step 1 · Inspect the branch the outer loop starts with

The outer loop's only input is the durable branch the previous
lesson's hand-off produced:

```bash
git -C work/hello-world-pico-sandcastle/target-repo \
    log --oneline sandcastle/hello-world-pico | head -5
```

Note in your walkthrough: *this branch is the entire interface
between the Sandcastle and everything that follows.* Everything the
outer loop does from here on can (and should) be reconstructed
from this branch alone.

Rule from [the lesson](index.qmd) being exercised: **the branch is
the only interface**.

## Step 2 · Read this repository's CI as the review-stage guardrail

The academy's own CI in
[`.github/workflows/build-and-publish.yml`](../../../../.github/workflows/build-and-publish.yml)
runs on every PR against `main` and builds the course sites. That
is a real example of an **automated-verification** guardrail
attached to the review stage — it lives in the environment
repository, not inside any Sandcastle.

Note in your walkthrough: *which parts of this workflow would you
extend to also re-run the hand-off's `verify.sh` on the merged
XR?* You do not have to implement it — the goal is to see where
the extension slot is.

Rule being exercised: **guardrails live outside the Sandcastle
boundary**.

## Step 3 · Read the merge stage as a policy, not a step

Open the repository on GitHub and inspect the branch-protection
rules on `main`. Merge is not a script you run — it is a policy
the environment repository enforces. In a real delivery setup, the
same policy would attach required reviewers, required checks, and
optionally a required signed commit.

Note in your walkthrough: *the outer loop's merge stage is a
policy configuration on the environment repository, not code that
lives in the Sandcastle or in the hand-off.*

Rule being exercised: **guardrails live outside the Sandcastle
boundary**.

## Step 4 · Map the GitOps delivery stage onto a manual apply

The academy does not yet ship a GitOps reconciler as part of a
runnable lab. The closest concrete equivalent you can inspect
today is the manual apply from the Kubernetes lab's own
walkthrough:

```bash
kubectl apply -f labs/hello-pico-on-kubernetes/downloads/05-xr.yaml
```

Read this line as *the reconciler's job on your behalf*. In a
real GitOps setup, Flux or Argo CD would watch the merged branch
and issue exactly this apply — with the added benefit that a
cluster-side admission policy (OPA / Kyverno) can reject the XR
before Crossplane sees it.

Note in your walkthrough: *the outer loop does not care whether
this apply is manual, GitOps-driven, or policy-gated — as long as
the XR that reaches the cluster is byte-equivalent to the one the
previous lesson's hand-off produced.*

Rule being exercised: **cluster reconciliation is Crossplane's
job**.

## Step 5 · Confirm Crossplane closes the loop

If you have the Crossplane cluster from the
[Hello Pico on Kubernetes walkthrough](../../../../labs/hello-pico-on-kubernetes/walkthrough.html)
running, reuse its `verify.sh` unchanged:

```bash
bash labs/hello-pico-on-kubernetes/downloads/verify.sh
```

Note in your walkthrough: *the same downstream verification
`verify.sh` works whether the XR arrived via a manual apply, a
GitOps sync, or a hypothetical future outer-loop lab.* That
independence is the outer loop's payoff.

Rule being exercised: **cluster reconciliation is Crossplane's
job**.

## Success criteria (paper walkthrough)

- [ ] You produced a one-page written map that annotates each of
      the four outer-loop stages with a concrete artifact you
      inspected in this repository or in the Kubernetes lab.
- [ ] Your map marks stages **0** (hand-off) and **4**
      (Crossplane reconciliation) as **runnable today**, and stages
      **1–3** (review, merge, GitOps delivery) as **inspectable
      but scaffolded**.
- [ ] You can name where a future runnable outer-loop lab would
      attach in each of the three scaffolded stages.
